narrative:
The model estimates you have a 48% chance of leaving your job. This is high enough that the company has decided to deny your promotion, as they are focusing opportunities on people more likely to stay long-term.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. Most influential was that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities strongly pushes the model toward expecting you will leave, even though most employees who stay (77%) report receiving no such offers. This factor alone pulled the prediction noticeably toward departure.

Working in your favor, your overall career experience of 6-10 years pushed the prediction back toward staying. While this is fairly common among people predicted to remain (35% of stayers have similar experience), it was the second strongest influence and helped reduce the likelihood of leaving.

Your time with this current organization (1-5 years) was the third most important factor. This shorter tenure in your present role also nudged the prediction toward leaving, as most employees the model expects to stay have been in their current job longer.

Taken together, the combination of external opportunities and relatively short time in this role outweighed your broader experience, leading to the decision. The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, while you may want to reflect on whether those outside offers better match your goals.
